newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: French workers protest at Dutch Akzo headquarters.
newsitem.headline: French workers protest at Dutch Akzo headquarters.

text.p: French employees at a unit of Dutch chemicals group Akzo Nobel travelled to the company's headquarters in Arnhem, Netherlands on Saturday to protest against proposed job cuts, the company said.

"There are around 350 people who arrived from France in eight buses. They marched from the central station to the headquarters and presented a petition to the company," Eduard Hirschfeld, head of Akzo corporate communications told Reuters.
Workers at the RETI drugs company of Riom in the French Auvergne region are protesting against a restructuring plan by Akzo which unions say would lead to 110 job losses.
Akzo said that of the 110 jobs, 50 would be moved to Paris and only the remaining 60 people would be affected by the plan.
In addition, Hirschfeld said that through internal re-organisation such as offers of early early retirement and job rotations the number of job losses could be further reduced.
"It will probably only be between 15 and 20 people, who will lose their jobs," he said.
A small delegation from the protestors met management and after brief talks the buses left for France, he added.
